newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Demand for Yugo T-bills good, BSE official.
newsitem.headline: Demand for Yugo T-bills good, BSE official.

text.p: The Yugoslav government sold 30 million dinars ($5.15 million) of its second issue of Treasury bills, the Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday.
The second issue, which had a volume of 200 million dinars, was launched on Thursday.
Thirty million sold were issued from the first 30-day tranche, which had a volume of 50 million dinars.
"Interest for the government bills is good, as it is safe to invest in them and because of their relatively short maturity," a BSE official said.
No bills from the 50-million dinar, second 60-day tranche or from the 100-million dinar, third 90-day tranche were sold.
The official said the bills' monthly interest rates dropped to 3.5 percent from a 4.5 percent on the first issue of government bills put on sale on May 12.
"The interest rates are on decline as the companies are not willing to pay a high price for the money and because of relative improvement of banks' liquidity."
A proportional method is applied for calculating the interest, the BSE said.
Companies can buy T-bills, issued at face value of 1,000 dinars, at the local bourse and from individuals through licenced banks. The bills can be used to pay customs and other import duties.
Bills from the first tranche can be used for customs payments 20 days after their primary sales, from the second tranche 30 days after and from the third tranche 45 days after their primary sales.
The government said earlier 200 million raised from the sale of the second T-bill issue will be used to meet the needs of the federal 1997 budget.
A hundred million dinars raised from the sale of the first issue of 30- and 60-day government T-bills will be used to finance the army's liabilities with commercial suppliers.
The fist issue of government T-bills was sold in the week ending June 27. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 311 4254
